paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of knowledge probing after editing with different methods on BioMedLM, as a function of co-occurrence number. The x-axis is scaled logarithmically and ranges from 10^0 to 10^3, with tick labels spaced by powers of 10 starting at 1 and ending at 1000. The y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %) and ranges from approximately 40% to 66%, with tick labels spaced by 5%. A black solid line represents the Base model, which begins at approximately 44% and plateaus at around 44% throughout the x-axis. A dark gray dashed line represents MEND, starting at approximately 48% and reaching around 56% at the highest co-occurrence number. A light gray solid line represents MEMIT, starting at approximately 49% and reaching approximately 55%. A green solid line represents IKE, beginning at approximately 43% and rising to approximately 52%. A blue solid line represents FT, starting at approximately 47% and increasing to approximately 50%. Finally, a reddish solid line represents ROME, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers.
